title: warranty_claim.evidence_incomplete payload
description:
A CONTROL, NOT A CONVENIENCE. P08 T-05 uses this event to SUPPRESS claim submission when the evidence pack is incomplete against the brand's own rules, and gate G4-02's 90% first-submission approval target rests on that suppression.

STATUS: NO MODULE PUBLISHES THIS EVENT. Audit AP-01 (critical, AUDIT-016) identified it; AR-009 §10.5 confirmed it still unpublished after measuring all 988 declared events; IN-003 §7.4 confirms it a third time at 2026-08-18. 'An architectural control that is documented and unpublished is not a control' (AR-009 §10.5).

The schema is issued here so that the gap is a missing EMITTER, not a missing DESIGN. Registering it is RE-02, a Wave 1 item ahead of the bulk remediation. The 422 rule.evidence_incomplete response it must produce is already specified in IN-002_artefacts/commercial/openapi.yaml (submitWarrantyClaim).

NAME: AP-01 called this 'claim.evidence_incomplete'. AR-008 §3 forbids the unqualified noun — 'claim' is ambiguous across warranty claims, insurance claims and marketplace disputes — so the registered name is qualified.

x-registration.comment_on_pii: none, deliberately. The payload names WHICH evidence items are absent, never their content, and carries no customer identifier — the claim id is sufficient for every consumer to resolve what it needs through an API. This keeps a high-frequency control event out of PDPA erasure scope entirely (IN-003 §4.3).
x-registration.comment_on_replay_class: R1. Re-evaluating completeness is idempotent and recomputable. It must NEVER acquire a side effect such as notifying the brand, which would make it R3 and unreplayable.

brand_code.description: The brand whose rule set was evaluated. Determines the data scope of every consumer — P08 sees only its own brand (AP-005 SC-02).

rule_set_version.description: The version of the BRAND'S evidence rule set that was applied. Required because a claim refused today and accepted tomorrow must be explainable by a rule change rather than by inconsistency — and because a brand disputing a suppression will ask which rules were in force.

missing.description: SC-06: enough for the consumer to act without a call-back. P08 renders this list directly to the brand partner, so each entry carries its own presentable label.

evidence_code.description: Controlled code for the evidence item, e.g. serial_plate_photograph.

requirement.description: conditional means required only because of another attribute of this claim; the reason is in condition_note.

rule.description: The 05-05 BRU- identifier. Machine-readable only — UI-004 E-06 forbids showing a rule identifier in user-facing text.

present_count.description: How many required items ARE present, so a progress indicator does not need a second call.

suppression.description: The control's effect, stated in the payload rather than inferred by each consumer — because two consumers inferring it differently is how a control becomes advisory.

rule_class.description: H hard block · A approved override · S soft warning · C computed. For evidence completeness this is H: no human can override it, because the brand will reject the claim regardless. This is the field that tells a caller whether anyone with authority can unblock them (AP-006 §4.2).

override_role.description: Null when rule_class is H. Present only where an approved override exists.

missing.condition_note: Required for intermittent-fault claims on this brand.
